items.originalTitle: On this day: Fernando Alonso wins the world title, Michael Schumacher retires from F1
items.summaryEn: On 22 October 2006, Fernando Alonso beat Michael Schumacher to the world title at the Brazilian Grand Prix, claiming his second F1 crown, as the seven-time champion Schumacher retired from Formula 1.
detailZh: 历史上的今天：费尔南多·阿隆索赢得世界冠军，迈克尔·舒马赫从F1退役
20年前，阿隆索夺得个人第二个F1世界冠军，舒马赫则告别了世界锦标赛
费尔南多·阿隆索，雷诺，迈克尔·舒马赫，法拉利
2006年10月22日，费尔南多·阿隆索在巴西大奖赛上击败迈克尔·舒马赫，夺得世界冠军；同日，七届世界冠军舒马赫从F1退役。
说实话，那天阿隆索几乎毫无疑问会锁定第二个总冠军头衔。舒马赫的引擎故障以及他在铃鹿站领先时退赛，将原本可能的两分领先变成了十分落后，这意味着这位法拉利车手既需要自己获胜，又需要对手在英特拉格斯不得分。
当舒马赫在第三节排位赛中遇到燃油压力问题、最终仅列第十位发车而阿隆索排在第四时，这一努力变得更加艰难。
“我不知道我们能做什么，”这位德国人在排位赛后说。“我不知道比赛会如何发展。很难预测什么，但我会尽我所能。从第十位起步要困难得多，但我当然会去尝试。”
“别忘了，过去迈克尔曾从更靠后的发车位赢下比赛，”法拉利技术总监罗斯·布朗补充道。
那个说法并不准确——在此前的248场比赛中，舒马赫仅有一次从前十名之外的位置夺冠——但这位法拉利车手恰恰证明了布朗为何会做出那样的判断。
他在第一圈就从第10位跃升至第7位，随后超越了前队友鲁本斯·巴里切罗，并在第八圈从外道超越吉安卡洛·费斯切拉升至第五——这意味着他已经紧追在自己的争冠对手身后——但与雷诺赛车的一次轻微触碰导致左后轮爆胎。
舒马赫跌至第20位，落后领跑的队友菲利佩·马萨69秒，而与阿隆索的差距恰好为一分钟。到第27圈时，他已经追上了队尾集团，并接连超越了蒂亚戈·蒙泰罗、罗伯特·杜恩博斯、尼克·海费尔德和罗伯特·库比卡，同时利用提前进站策略超越其他对手并受益于对手退赛，在第二次进站前已升至第五位。
重新出站后他位列第七，舒马赫再次超越巴里切罗，并在第一弯迫使费斯切拉锁死轮胎，于第63圈夺得第五位。马萨强势的主场表现意味着他仍领先33秒，但排名第二的阿隆索距离正在追赶的法拉利赛车仅差八秒。
舒马赫未能获得登上领奖台所需的圈数，但在倒数第三圈对迈凯伦车队的基米·莱科宁完成了一次干净利落的超越，升至第四名，而阿隆索则锁定了年度冠军。
费尔南多·阿隆索，雷诺车队；迈克尔·舒马赫，法拉利车队
“这场比赛一片混乱，我觉得这个词用得恰当，”舒马赫说。“我们今天确实拥有一辆极佳的赛车，从纯速度来看我们本可以套所有人一圈。所以我必须说，就赛车性能而言这是赛季的完美收官，但对我来说结果并不理想。”
阿隆索称赞这是结束他在雷诺时光的“绝佳方式”，他将雷诺描述为“我在一级方程式中的家”，随后他将转投迈凯伦，这一转会早已备受期待，他将于2007年加盟。
“我会一生都带着与他们的这些回忆，以这样的方式结束最后一场比赛是你做梦都想不到的，你甚至不会去尝试梦想，因为它总是超出你的预期，”他评论道。
沿着那条职业道路，这位西班牙人梦想着效仿艾尔顿·塞纳。“加入迈凯伦而从未与法拉利一起比赛，让我想起了很多塞纳，”他告诉西班牙电视五台。“他赢得了三个冠军，对我来说，带着三个冠军退役并实现他所实现的成就，将是我职业生涯的目标。”二十年过去了，阿隆索仍在F1中追逐那第三个冠军。
与此同时，舒马赫在蒙扎宣布退役一个月后，回顾了他辉煌的职业生涯。
随着法拉利为2007年签下莱科宁，舒马赫留下将要以年轻车手马萨为代价，所以他决定不这么做。但未来他有可能回归吗？
“一级方程式赛车一直在变，”这位37岁的车手回答道。“技术、引擎、规则、赛道。一旦你离开，就是离开了。”
最终，竞争的吸引力实在太大，舒马赫于2010年至2012年重返梅赛德斯，度过了三年时光。在此期间，他难以与队友尼科·罗斯伯格匹敌，仅收获一次领奖台，并在最后一次摩纳哥出战中拿下杆位。
但在舒马赫阵营中，他首次退役时的一大感受也是如释重负。
当德国电视台RTL问她什么让她感到幸福时，他的妻子科琳娜·舒马赫回答道：“我们都能健康地回家，这些年什么都没发生，我们只付出了一条腿骨折的代价就挺过来了。”
不幸的是，尽管这位七届世界冠军在赛车生涯中安然无恙，但他在2013年12月的一次滑雪事故中受了重伤。现年55岁的他，自那以后就再未公开露面。
detailEn: On this day: Fernando Alonso wins the world title, Michael Schumacher retires from F1
20 years ago, Alonso claimed his second F1 title as Schumacher bowed out from the world championship
Fernando Alonso, Renault, Michael Schumacher, Ferrari
On 22 October 2006, Fernando Alonso beat Michael Schumacher to the world title in the Brazilian Grand Prix, as the seven-time champion retired from Formula 1.

In truth, there was little doubt Alonso was going to clinch a second crown that day. Schumacher’s engine failure and retirement from the lead of the Suzuka race had turned a potential two-point lead into a 10-point deficit, meaning the Ferrari racer needed both to win and his rival not to score at Interlagos.
That endeavour took a turn for the worse when Schumacher encountered a fuel pressure problem in Q3, leaving him 10th on the grid with Alonso fourth.

“I don't know what we can do,” the German said after qualifying. “I don't know how the race will develop. It is hard to predict something, but I will try my best. It is much more difficult starting from 10th, but of course I will try.”
“Let's not forget that in the past, Michael has managed to win races starting even further back on the grid,” Ferrari technical director Ross Brawn added.
That statement was inaccurate – across the preceding 248 races, Schumacher had won from outside the top 10 just once – but the Ferrari driver showed exactly why Brawn made it.

He jumped from 10th to seventh on the first lap, then passed former team-mate Rubens Barrichello and overtook Giancarlo Fisichella around the outside for fifth on lap eight – meaning he was already right behind his title rival – but the slightest of touches with the Renault caused a rear-left puncture.

Schumacher found himself down in 20th, 69 seconds adrift of race-leading team-mate Felipe Massa, while his deficit to Alonso was exactly one minute. By lap 27, he had caught the back of the pack and successively overtook Tiago Monteiro, Robert Doornbos, Nick Heidfeld and Robert Kubica, while undercutting other opponents and benefitting from retirements, to find himself fifth before his second pitstop.

Emerging back out in seventh, Schumacher passed Barrichello again and pressured Fisichella into a lock-up in Turn 1 to claim fifth on lap 63. Massa’s commanding home drive meant he was still 33 seconds up the road, but second-placed Alonso was just eight seconds away from the recovering Ferrari.

Schumacher ran out of laps to claim a podium finish but still performed a clinical move on McLaren’s Kimi Raikkonen on the antepenultimate lap to take fourth position, as Alonso secured the championship.
Fernando Alonso, Renault, Michael Schumacher, Ferrari

“The race was chaotic, I think that is the right word,” Schumacher said. “We really had a superb car today, from the pure speed we could have lapped everybody. So I have to say it was the perfect end to the season in terms of car performance, but for me it didn't work out well.”
Alonso hailed a “fantastic way” to conclude his time at Renault, which he described as “my family in Formula 1”, ahead of his long-awaited move to McLaren for 2007.

“I will have these memories with them all my life, and to finish the last race like this is something that you never dream of, you never even try to dream of, because it's always more than what you expected,” he commented.

With that career path, the Spaniard dreamt of emulating Ayrton Senna. “To join McLaren and never to race with Ferrari reminds me a lot of Senna,” he told TV channel Telecinco. “He won three titles, and for me, to retire with three and achieve what he achieved would be the objective of my career.” Twenty years on, Alonso is still chasing that third crown in F1.
Meanwhile, Schumacher looked back on his glittering career, one month after announcing his retirement in Monza.
With Ferrari signing Raikkonen for 2007, Schumacher staying would have come at the expense of youngster Massa, so he decided against it. But was there any chance he could return in the future?
“Formula 1 is constantly changing,” the 37-year-old responded. “The technology, the engines, the rules, the circuits. Once you're out of it, you're out.”

In the end, the attraction of competition proved too strong and Schumacher returned for a three-year stint at Mercedes from 2010 to 2012, during which he struggled to match team-mate Nico Rosberg and scored just one podium finish while topping qualifying on his last Monaco outing.
But in the Schumacher camp, one major feeling when he first retired also was relief.

When asked by German network RTL what made her happy, his wife, Corinna Schumacher, replied: “That we're all going to go home healthy, that nothing happened in all these years and that we got away with just the one broken leg.”

Unfortunately, while the seven-time world champion emerged unscathed from his racing career, he was severely injured in a skiing accident in December 2013. Now 55 years old, he has not been seen in public since then.

keyPointsEn: Schumacher's engine failure and retirement from the lead at Suzuka turned a potential two-point lead into a 10-point deficit.

items.originalTitle: MotoGP can’t simply copy F1’s Drive to Survive success – Chase Carey
items.summaryEn: Liberty Media director Chase Carey believes MotoGP cannot simply copy Netflix's Formula 1 docuseries Drive to Survive in order to gain widespread recognition. Liberty acquired F1 in January 2017, and the show's first season, released two years later, substantially contributed to the championship's increased popularity.
detailZh: MotoGP不能简单复制F1《极速求生》的成功——蔡斯·凯里
Liberty Media董事谈如何发展MotoGP——走一条与F1不同的道路
Liberty Media董事蔡斯·凯里认为，MotoGP“不能简单照搬”Netflix的F1纪录片《极速求生》来获得广泛认可。
Liberty于2017年1月收购F1，这家美国公司主导下的重大事件之一，是两年后Netflix该纪录片首季的上线，这大幅提升了这项世界锦标赛的受欢迎程度。
自由媒体随后于2025年7月收购了现称为84%的股份。该集团正寻求让摩托车大奖赛更加多元化——2026年MotoGP锦标赛排名前12的车手中，有11名是西班牙人或意大利人——同时增加其在美国的影响力。
“当然，MotoGP车队需要做的一些事情与一级方程式有相似之处，”凯里在纽约举行的Autosport Business Exchange会议上表示。“显然，这是一个全球性的特许经营赛事。”
“现在还为时过早。他们正在努力推进，制定战略和机会，思考如何像我们在一级方程式中所尝试的那样，将这项运动发展壮大。”
《极速求生》被认为将一级方程式介绍给了全新的观众群体，而新冠疫情封锁措施则起到了助推作用——第一季封锁恰好在第二季播出几周后发生。
“《求生之路》可能是最明显的例子，”凯里承认。“我们意识到，我们需要拥有构成这项运动的个性人物，给他们更大的平台，让车迷参与进来。
“如今的数字世界是一个全天候的世界。高端的体验仍然是现场比赛，但归根结底，人们是在与比赛建立联系，关注比赛和比赛片段，关注人们在做什么的片段，以及幕后发生的事情。
“他们全天候关注这些。所以我们需要继续寻找方法，满足这种渴望和与他们的运动建立联系的愿望，提供让车迷以这种方式与运动建立联系的载体。
“目前美国是我们这项运动最大的YouTube市场。所以这告诉了你我们通过[这些]载体所建立的联系。”
“《极速求生》已成为数字化工作的核心。数字化方面有很多工作在进行，但这无疑是核心。对我们来说，这是一个极其重要、极具价值的系列。”
许多赛事，无论是赛车运动还是其他领域，都试图效仿这一成功，但凯里认为这对MotoGP来说并不合适。
“你应该寻找机会，”这位美国人坚持道。“现实情况是，所有人都看了《极速求生》，然后所有人都试图去做。高尔夫尝试了他们的《全力挥杆》，网球尝试了《破发点》——所有人都是如此。
“通常，你不能只是照搬。我认为我们在福克斯电视台做《美国偶像》时就学到了这一点。《美国偶像》在某种程度上激发了全世界的想象力，之后也有一些节目跟进并做得不错，但真正能做到这一点的只有一个《美国偶像》。
我认为一般来说，你不能只是照搬同样的做法出去做。你必须找到方法去利用机会、利用个性、利用数字平台、发展优秀的合作伙伴。
像苹果这样的一级方程式合作伙伴，我认为这正是苹果为如何转播以及与车迷建立联系带来了全新视角的地方。所以我认为这类机会，你必须接着看看你能用它做什么、如何发展它。
他们必须走自己的路，找到自己的机会。一级方程式电影就是一个很好的机会，但你不能只是出去拍一部MotoGP电影。那可能并不是合适的机会。
但也许还有别的东西——一定会有别的东西。这大概不只是做你以前做过的同样的事情，而是找到那些机会、找到那些个性。
detailEn: MotoGP can’t simply copy F1’s Drive to Survive success – Chase Carey
Liberty Media director weighs in on how to grow MotoGP – with a different path to F1’s
Liberty Media director Chase Carey believes MotoGP “can’t just copy” Netflix’s Formula 1 docuseries Drive to Survive to gain widespread recognition.

Liberty acquired F1 in January 2017, and one of the major events under the American company was the release of the Netflix show’s opening season two years later, which substantially contributed to the world championship’s increased popularity.

Liberty then bought 84% of Dorna Sports (now known as MotoGP Sports Entertainment Group) in July 2025. The group is seeking to make motorcycle grands prix more diverse – 11 of the top 12 riders in the 2026 MotoGP championship are Spanish or Italian – while increasing its presence in the United States.

“Certainly there are elements of what teams need to do in MotoGP that will have similarities to Formula 1,” Carey said in a conference at Autosport Business Exchange in New York. “Obviously, it is a global franchise.
“It's early days. They're working on it, developing the strategies, the opportunities of how you take that sport and grow it in the way we've tried to with Formula 1.”
Drive to Survive has been credited with introducing F1 to a brand-new audience, boosted by the COVID-19 pandemic’s lockdowns, which first occurred a couple of weeks after season two was released.

“Drive to Survive is probably the most obvious example,” Carey acknowledged. “We recognised we needed to have the personalities that make up the sport, give them a bigger platform and let fans engage.

“The digital world today is a 24/7 world. The premium experience is still that live race, but at the end of the day people are connecting with the race, following the race and clips of the race, clips of what people are doing, things going on behind the scenes.

“They're following that 24/7. So we need to continue to find ways to feed that appetite and that desire to connect with their sport, provide the vehicles that enable fans to connect with the sport in that way.
“Right now the US is the biggest YouTube market for our sport. So it tells you about the connection we're having through [those] vehicles.

“Drive to Survive has become a centerpiece in the digital efforts. A lot of efforts are going on with digital, but that certainly is the centerpiece. It has been an incredibly important, valuable franchise for us.”
Many competitions, in motorsport and beyond, have attempted to emulate this success, but Carey doesn’t believe that would be right for MotoGP.

“You should look for opportunities,” the American insisted. “Realistically, everybody saw Drive to Survive and then everybody tried to do it. Golf tried to do their Full Swing, tennis tried to do Break Point – everybody.

“Usually, you can't just copy something. I think we learned that at Fox with American Idol. American Idol sort of captured the world's imagination, and there were shows that came behind and did well, but there was only one American Idol that really did that.
“I think generally you can't go out and do the same thing. You've got to find ways to use opportunities, use personalities, use digital platforms, develop great partners.

“A partner in Formula 1 like Apple, I think this is where Apple has brought a whole new perspective to how you broadcast and connect with fans. So I think that type of opportunity, you've got to then see what you can do with it, how you develop it.

“They have to follow their own path and find their own opportunities. The Formula 1 movie was a great opportunity for that, but you can't just go out and do a MotoGP movie. That may not be the right opportunity.
“But there may be something else – there will be something else. It's probably not just doing the same things you did, it's finding those opportunities, finding those personalities.”
keyPointsZh: 《极速求生》首季在收购两年后上线，大幅提升了F1的受欢迎程度
keyPointsEn: The first season of Drive to Survive was released two years after the acquisition and substantially contributed to F1's increased popularity.

items.originalTitle: Red Bull called Christian Horner to thank him for F1 engine project after maiden win
items.summaryEn: Christian Horner has revealed that Red Bull shareholders called him to thank him for his contribution to the Red Bull Ford Powertrains engine project after its maiden Formula 1 victory in Malaysia. Horner joined the Milton Keynes-based team as team principal ahead of the 2005 season and was sacked in July 2025, replaced by Laurent Mekies.
detailZh: 红牛股东致电克里斯蒂安·霍纳，感谢他为F1引擎项目所做的贡献
前车队领队对红牛当前成功的贡献得到了认可
克里斯蒂安·霍纳透露，红牛福特动力总成引擎在马来西亚取得F1首胜后，红牛股东致电感谢他。
霍纳是在红牛收购捷豹车队后、2005赛季前加入这支位于米尔顿凯恩斯的车队担任领队的，但于2025年7月被解雇，由洛朗·梅基斯接任。
在执掌车队的二十年里，霍纳不仅带领车队拿下八个车手总冠军和六个车队总冠军，还在本田于2021赛季末退出F1后，主导了车队从引擎客户向动力单元制造商的转型。
红牛得以继续使用日本动力单元直到去年；其与福特合作设计的自有动力单元于2026年首次亮相。
红牛引擎在马来西亚巴林大奖赛上由马克斯·维斯塔潘拿下首胜，一周后荷兰人在新加坡实现背靠背夺冠。
“我们在底盘方面做到了，随后挑战来了：我们能在引擎方面也做到吗？”霍纳在纽约Autosport Business Exchange的一次会议上说道。
“你知道，在2020年本田宣布退出后，我们必须要有引擎。所以我们创立了这家名为动力总成的初创公司，秉持同样的理念——吸引人才、给人们机会和机遇，并赋能他们、鼓励他们突破边界。”
“能成为今年研发并交付的这款引擎的一部分，我感到无比自豪。”
霍纳的贡献得到了品牌本身的认可，他接到了品牌领导层打来的上述电话。
“看到那台引擎并知道它凝聚了多少心血，你知道，一路上的汗水与泪水，这是一个令人感激的举动，”这位英国人继续说道。
“对所有参与其中的男男女女来说，这是一项令人难以置信、难以置信的成就。即使在最好的时候，赢得一场大奖赛也非常艰难。
“我非常感激两位主动联系我的股东，也感激所有主动联系我、向我表示感谢的男男女女。那通电话与我15个月前接到的那通电话截然不同。”
霍纳指的是导致他被解雇的那通电话，因为在红牛联合创始人迪特里希·马特希茨去世后，他的职位变得越来越岌岌可危。
克里斯蒂安·霍纳，红牛车队领队，与迪特里希·马特希茨，红牛首席执行官兼创始人
霍纳没有得到维斯塔潘阵营的支持，并且正在失去尤维迪亚家族的支持——查勒姆·尤维迪亚是该公司的大股东——但他仍将这一消息描述为“相当突然且相当残酷”。
“我觉得事情正在发生变化，”他补充道。“没有什么会永远保持不变，而且在创始人迪特里希·马特希茨于22年底不幸去世后，公司注定会演变或发生变化。
“迪特里希，他就是红牛，他是所有重大决策背后的力量。而突然间，显然，试图取代这样一个人是不可能的。
“然后显然，随着集团的发展并承担起这一挑战，情况就不同了。有一股力量要将更多控制权收回总部，这与我们在红牛车队所享有的自主权截然不同。
“这基本上与我们原本走的路线不同，而你能感觉到那种变化正在发生。这并不是说它对或错，只是不同而已。”
“所以，不可避免地，事情陷入了僵局。”
detailEn: Red Bull called Christian Horner to thank him for F1 engine project after maiden win
Former team boss’s contribution to Red Bull’s current success has been acknowledged
Christian Horner has revealed Red Bull shareholders called him on the back of the Red Bull Ford Powertrains engine’s maiden Formula 1 victory in Malaysia.
Horner joined the Milton Keynes-based squad as its team principal when the brand acquired the Jaguar outfit ahead of the 2005 season, but was sacked and replaced by Laurent Mekies in July 2025.

Across two decades at the helm of the team, Horner not only led it to eight drivers’ and six constructors’ titles but also oversaw its transition from an engine customer into a power unit manufacturer, following Honda’s exit from F1 at the end of the 2021 season.
Red Bull was able to keep using the Japanese powertrains until last year; its own power unit, designed in collaboration with Ford, debuted in 2026.
The Red Bull engine clinched its first victory at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, courtesy of Max Verstappen, with the Dutchman making it back-to-back wins one week later in Singapore.
“We managed to do it on the chassis side and then the challenge came, could we do it on the engine side?” Horner related in a conference at Autosport Business Exchange in New York.

“You know, we needed to have an engine after Honda announced their withdrawal in 2020. So we created this start-up company called Powertrains, with the same philosophy of attracting the talent, giving people the chances and giving people the opportunity, and empowering them and encouraging them to push the boundaries.
“I've been super proud to be a part of the engine that was developed and delivered this year.”
Horner’s contribution was acknowledged by the brand itself, as he received the aforementioned phone call from its leaders.
“It was an appreciated gesture, seeing that engine and knowing what went into it, you know, the sweat and tears along the way,” the Briton continued.
“For all the men and women involved, it was an incredible, incredible achievement. To win a grand prix is very hard at the best times.
“I was very grateful to both the shareholders who reached out, and all of the men and women who reached out to thank me as well. It was quite a different call to the one I had 15 months earlier.”
Horner is referring to the phone call that led to his dismissal, as his position had become increasingly precarious following Red Bull cofounder Dietrich Mateschitz’s death.
Christian Horner, Red Bull Racing Team Principal and Dietrich Mateschitz, CEO and Founder of Red Bull

Horner did not have the Verstappen camp on his side and was losing the support of the Yoovidhya family – Chalerm Yoovidhya is a majority owner of the company – but still describes the news as “pretty abrupt and quite brutal”.

“I felt that things were changing,” he added. “Nothing stays the same forever, and after the founder Dietrich Mateschitz sadly passed at the end of ‘22, it was always going to be the case that the company was going to evolve or was going to change.
“Dietrich, he was Red Bull, he was the power behind all big decisions. And suddenly, obviously, trying to replace somebody like that, it’s impossible.

“And then obviously, as the group evolved and took on that challenge, it was just different. There was a drive to bring more control back into the head office and that sat differently from the autonomy that we'd enjoyed at Red Bull Racing.
“It was a different path than essentially what we were on, and you could feel that that was changing. It wasn't that it was right or wrong, it was just different.
“So, inevitably, it came to a deadlock.”

items.originalTitle: Cadillac unveils $222,500 Sergio Perez special-edition ahead of 300th F1 start
detailZh: 凯迪拉克在墨西哥城大奖赛之前发布了价值222,500美元的塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯特别版Escalade-V车型，以庆祝其300次F1赛事的启动
凯迪拉克为其F1车手塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯推出了一款独家版的682马力Escalade-V车型，以庆祝墨西哥城大奖赛
赛车文化超越赛道。车手生活方式、时尚、旅行、设计和那些让赛车不仅仅是一项运动的故事
汽车制造商凯迪拉克为了纪念其F1车手塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯，推出了一款特别版的Escalade-V。仅生产11辆，以庆祝车手的赛车号码
名为Escalade-V Checo Perez版的SUV现在在墨西哥的经销商处有售，售价为409.9万比索——约合22.25万美元。这比该国目前销售的普通版本高出约25万比索。
除了在车身某处有F1车手的名字外，你还能得到什么？
正如你所期望的，变化主要是外观上的，Escalade和V系列标志以黑色完成，加上与MAC-26 F1赛车颜色相呼应的黑白凯迪拉克标志。格栅和车门把手都带有照明，打开引擎盖将揭示一个碳纤维引擎盖。
车轮是24英寸的磨砂石墨单元。
内饰也进行了一些小改动，配备了运动踏板和与车队相同的单色主题装饰。B柱和中央控制台上两个编号的铭牌告诉你你购买的是哪一辆，佩雷斯签名的标志旁边提醒你为什么最初会购买这款车。
从性能角度来看，没有任何变化。6.2升V8发动机仍然采用涡轮增压，功率为682马力，扭矩为653磅英尺，通过10速自动变速箱传递到所有四个车轮。60英里每小时可以在4.4秒内完成，虽然不如F1赛车快，但对于公路使用来说已经足够快了。
新车发布在佩雷斯家乡赛事墨西哥城大奖赛之前，紧接着本周末在奥斯汀的赛事。这将是他第300次大奖赛发车。
但36岁的佩雷斯暗示他的F1生涯即将结束。本周他与墨西哥广播公司Televisa交谈时表示，凯迪拉克的项目“需要比我想象的更多时间”。
“我认为给出具体年份是困难的，但不会太久，”佩雷斯说。 “真正让我犹豫不决（继续）的是我的孩子们。”
他补充说： “我希望在一级方程式赛车的生涯中画上一个圆满的句号，我所能说的是，我们很快就会知道（我何时退休）。
detailEn: Cadillac unveils $222,500 Sergio Perez special-edition ahead of 300th F1 start
Cadillac has unveiled an exclusive Sergio Perez edition of its 682hp Escalade-V ahead of the Mexico City Grand Prix
Motorsport culture beyond the track. Driver lifestyle, fashion, travel, design and the stories that make racing more than a sport.
Car manufacturer Cadillac has launched a special edition Escalade-V in the name of its Formula 1 driver Sergio Perez. Just 11 will be made, in celebration of the driver's race number.

Aptly named the Escalade-V Checo Perez Edition, the SUV is now on sale in dealers throughout Mexico with a purchase rice of 4,099,000 pesos - or around $222,500. This is roughly 250,000 pesos more than the standard version currently for sale in the country.
So what do you get apart from an F1 driver's name scribbled somewhere on the bodywork?

As you would expect, the changes are mostly cosmetic, with the Escalade and V-Series badges finished in black, plus a monochrome Cadillac logo mirroring the colours of the MAC-26 F1 car. The grille and door handles are illuminated, and lifting the bonnet will reveal a carbon fibre engine cover.
Wheels are 24-inch Satin Graphite units.

The interior also gets a minor makeover, with sports pedals and trim coloured in the same monochrome theme as the team. Two numbered plaques on the B-pillar and centre console tell you which of the 11 you have purchased, and Perez's signature sat next to the number reminds you why you made the purchase in the first place.

From a performance point of view, nothing changes at all. The 6.2-litre V8 still comes supercharged to the tune of 682hp and 653lb-ft of torque, which is sent through a 10-speed automatic gearbox to all four wheels. 60mph comes and goes in 4.4 seconds - not quite as fast as an F1 car, but plenty for road use.
The launch comes ahead of Perez’s home race, the Mexico City Grand Prix, which follows this weekend’s round in Austin. It will be his 300th grand prix start.

But the 36-year-old has hinted that the end of his F1 career is getting closer. Speaking to Mexican broadcaster Televisa this week, he said Cadillac’s project “requires more time than I initially thought”.
“I think giving a specific number [of years] is difficult, but it won’t be much longer,” Perez said. “What really holds me back [from continuing] is my kids.”
He added: “I want to finish my time in Formula 1 on a high note, and all I can say is that we will know when [I retire] soon.”

items.titleZh: 霍纳回忆录披露五件鲜为人知往事
items.summaryZh: 克里斯蒂安·霍纳的回忆录《Drive》今日发行，讲述他从立志成为F1车手到成为最成功车队领队之一的经历。The Race在专访前通读全书，选出五件引人注目且此前鲜为人知的事情。
items.originalTitle: Five surprising things we learned from Horner's book
items.summaryEn: Christian Horner's memoir 'Drive' is released today, telling the story of how he started out as an aspiring Formula 1 driver before becoming one of the most successful team bosses of all time. Ahead of its extensive interview with Horner, The Race read every page and picked out five attention-grabbing and previously little-known things.
detailZh: 克里斯蒂安·霍纳的回忆录《Drive》今日发行，讲述了他从立志成为F1车手起步、最终成为史上最成功车队领队之一的经历。
在上周对克里斯蒂安·霍纳进行长篇专访之前（专访内容可在YouTube和播客中获取），我们读完了全书每一页，挑选出五件引人注目、且此前鲜为人知的事情。
1 霍纳曾以青训车手身份测试劳伦斯·斯特罗尔的F1赛车
霍纳参加F3时曾短暂签约路特斯，身份就是如今所说的青训车手。这需要付出代价：一笔17万英镑的“年费”，霍纳称自己为此艰难筹款，据信某位名叫奈杰尔·曼塞尔的人提供了一点帮助。
他当时正努力成为职业赛车手，只得到过一次驾驶F1赛车的机会，那是在赫瑟尔测试赛道上对一辆已卖给劳伦斯·斯特罗尔（现阿斯顿·马丁F1车队联合所有者）的莲花赛车进行试车。
“引擎轰然启动的声音差点让我心脏病发作，”霍纳写道。“它的动力令人难以置信，也令人畏惧。那辆莲花赛车的一切似乎都随时会爆炸。
“底盘愤怒地颤抖，我的双手在方向盘上震动。就像我被绑在一艘火箭飞船的前端，在几圈短暂的驾驶中，加速时我的头猛地撞向头枕；刹车时，我的肋骨感到被挤压，因为我被向前推在座椅上，又猛地撞回安全带。
“之后我的眼睛一定瞪得像碟子一样大。我感到亢奋。F1赛车的动力似乎无穷无尽。”
那件事，再加上一个国际F3000赛季，就是他以职业车手身份最接近F1的时候了。
2 劳达曾邀请霍纳出任梅赛德斯车队领队
当霍纳正带领红牛度过他们在F1的首个统治期时，2012年底尼基·劳达找上门来，请他接任梅赛德斯车队领队。
“圣诞假期期间，尼基来到我家，请我加入梅赛德斯担任他的车队领队，”霍纳写道。“我一时措手不及。离开红牛从来都
这件事曾在我脑海中闪过。当他随后列出一连串令人眼花缭乱的数字时，我意识到他正在讨论我的潜在薪资。
霍纳声称他拒绝了这份邀约，理由是他从零开始打造了红牛车队，并且对红牛和迪特里希·马特希茨忠心耿耿。随后，托托·沃尔夫被任命担任该职位。
3 库特哈德可能保住了霍纳在红牛的饭碗
红牛最初与霍纳的合同包括两年期限以及2007年的续约选项。但他在书中解释道，在2006年摩纳哥大奖赛之前，他通过赫尔穆特·马尔科得知，预计这个选项不会被激活——这一点后来被一封信所证实。
“没有解释为什么会这样，”霍纳写道。“我感到措手不及，但我没有变得沮丧，而是专注于比赛，并想好了下一步该怎么走。”
结果下一步是库特哈德在摩纳哥以第三名拿下红牛在F1的首个领奖台。库特哈德并不知道幕后这一情况是如何发展的，因此他在确保霍纳留任方面发挥了重要作用。
霍纳的回忆录中对马尔科有不少批评，尽管也对他最初将自己引入担任车队领队一职心存感激。一个关键方面是马尔科对媒体的言论在多大程度上让阿德里安·纽维感到沮丧。
“他的媒体活动同样令人沮丧，因为他乐于向他偏爱的平台分享内部信息，”霍纳写道。“除了呈现一个自我标榜的
他在媒体面前以权威姿态发声，对红牛的车手、赛车、工程师、策略以及与我们竞赛方式有关的一切事务直言不讳，这些观点都被公之于众。
霍纳形容纽维“随着每一次泄密变得越来越焦躁”，因为他不愿不必要地泄露任何技术机密。
5 里卡多退出了与红牛的口头协议
当丹尼尔·里卡多在2018年匈牙利大奖赛后打电话告诉霍纳“我要去雷诺”时，人们感到沮丧。尤其是因为红牛已经同意了里卡多的所有条件——一份为期一年的合同，以及不逊于雷诺提供的每年2500万美元的薪酬。
“我感到非常失望，”霍纳写道。“迪特里希给丹尼尔提供了一份很棒的合同；已经握手敲定了。现在他却要离开我们去雷诺，而包括迈凯伦在内的其他几支更优秀的车队都想签下他。这一切对我来说都说不通。”
霍纳认为，里卡多做出这一选择的关键原因，是需要离开一支已被马克斯·维斯塔潘打上个人烙印的车队。
detailEn: Christian Horner's memoir ‘Drive' is released today, telling the story of how he started out as an aspiring Formula 1 driver before becoming one of the most successful team bosses of all time.

Prior to our extensive interview with Christian Horner last week, which is available both on YouTube and in podcast form, we read every page and have picked out five attention-grabbing - and previously little-known - things that caught our eye.
1 Horner tested Lawrence Stroll's F1 car as a junior

When he was racing in Formula 3, Horner was briefly on Lotus's books as what we'd today call a junior driver. This came with a price, with a £170,000 "annual fee" that Horner explains battling to raise - with a little help suspected to have come from a certain Nigel Mansell.

He only had one opportunity to drive an F1 car while trying to become a professional racing driver when he shook down a Lotus that had been sold to Lawrence Stroll, now Aston Martin F1 co-owner, at the Hethel test track.
"The sound of the engine exploding into life had nearly given me a heart attack," writes Horner. "Its power felt incredible and intimidating. Everything about the Lotus seemed primed to explode.

"The chassis trembled angrily and my hands vibrated on the steering wheel. It was as if I'd been strapped to the front of a rocket ship, and during several brief laps, my head snapped back against the headrest when accelerating; during braking, my ribs felt compressed as I was thrust forward in my seat and bucked against the harness.
"My eyes must have looked like saucers afterwards. I felt high. The power of a Formula 1 car seemed limitless."
That, and a season in International F3000, was as close as he got to F1 as a professional driver.
2 Lauda offered Horner the Mercedes team boss job
When Horner was in the middle of leading Red Bull's first spell of F1 dominance, he was approached by Niki Lauda to take over as Mercedes team principal in late 2012.
"During the Christmas break, Niki came to my house and asked me to join Mercedes as his team principal," writes Horner. "I was caught off guard. Leaving Red Bull had never
crossed my mind. When he then laid out a series of dazzling numbers, I realised he was discussing my potential salary."
Horner claims to have turned down the offer, citing how he had built Red Bull Racing from scratch and his loyalty to Red Bull and Dietrich Mateschitz. Toto Wolff was then appointed to the role.
3 Coulthard may have saved Horner's Red Bull job

Red Bull's original deal with Horner comprised two years and an option for 2007. But he explains in his book how he heard via Helmut Marko ahead of the 2006 Monaco Grand Prix that this option was not expected to be picked up - something that was later confirmed by a letter.
"There was no explanation for why," writes Horner. "I felt blindsided, but rather than becoming despondent, I focused on the race and worked out my next steps."

It turns out that the next step was Coulthard taking the first Red Bull podium in F1 with third place in Monaco. Coulthard, who was unaware of how this situation played out behind the scenes, therefore played an important role in ensuring Horner stayed on.

There's plenty of criticism of Marko in Horner's memoir, albeit offset by gratitude for his role in bringing him in as team principal in the first place. One key aspect is the extent to which Marko's comments to the media frustrated Adrian Newey.
"His media activities were equally frustrating because he happily shared insider information with the platforms he favoured," writes Horner. "Aside from presenting a self-styled

position of authority to the media, his outspoken opinions about Red Bull's drivers, cars, engineers, strategies and anything and everything to do with our racing approach were being announced to the world."
Horner describes Newey as growing "more agitated with every leak", given his desire not to give away any technical secrets unnecessarily.
5 Ricciardo walked out of a handshake deal with Red Bull

When Daniel Ricciardo called Horner to tell him that "I'm going to Renault" after the 2018 Hungarian Grand Prix, there was frustration. Not least because Red Bull had agreed to all of Ricciardo's terms with a one-year deal and a pay packet no worse than the $25million a year he was offered by Renault.

"I felt so disappointed," writes Horner. "Dietrich had offered Daniel a great deal; it had been agreed with a handshake. Now he was leaving us for Renault, when several other superior teams, McLaren included, wanted to sign him. None of it made sense to me."
Horner suggests the need to get out of a team Max Verstappen had made his own was key to Ricciardo's choice.
